question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The manager remained calmly (a)/ even when the angry crowd (b)/ surrounded his car. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Remain" is a linking verb here: it shows the state of the subject and not an action. A linking verb is followed by an adjective, so "remained calmly" must be "remained calm".

◦ Corrected sentence: The manager remained calm even when the angry crowd surrounded his car.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "even when the angry crowd" is a proper clause of concession, and "angry" correctly describes the noun "crowd".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "surrounded his car" is a proper past verb phrase with a correct object.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because the adverb "calmly" after the linking verb "remained" in part (a) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• Linking verbs — be, seem, appear, become, remain, stay, look, feel, sound, taste, smell, grow, turn — take an adjective: She stayed quiet, He grew angry. With an action verb, the adverb is used: He spoke calmly.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Among all the hotels in the town, (a)/ this one is the (b)/ cleanest and (c)/ the most cheapest. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A superlative is formed either with "-est" or with "most", and never with both. "Cheapest" already ends in "-est", so "the most cheapest" must be "the cheapest".

◦ Corrected sentence: Among all the hotels in the town, this one is the cleanest and the cheapest.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Among all the hotels in the town," is a proper introductory phrase, and "among" suits more than two.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "this one is the" is a proper singular subject with the correct verb and article.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "cleanest and" is a proper superlative, formed with "-est".

 

NOTE

 

• most cheapest, most best, most largest, more better are all double forms. Use one marker only: the cheapest or the most expensive.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Of the five chapters in this book, (a)/ the latter (b)/ is the most difficult. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The latter" (like "the former") is used only when two things have been mentioned. Here five chapters are named, so the correct word is "the last".

◦ Corrected sentence: Of the five chapters in this book, the last is the most difficult.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Of the five chapters in this book," is a proper introductory phrase that names the group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "is the most difficult" is a proper superlative predicate, and "most" is right for a long adjective.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "the latter" in part (b) is incorrect for a group of five.

 

NOTE

 

• former / latter — used for two items; first / last — used for three or more: Of the three, the first was… the last was….

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Because of dense fog, (a)/ the flights were delayed and (b)/ much of the passengers were stranded. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Much" is used with uncountable nouns, and "many" with countable plural nouns. "Passengers" is countable, so "much of the passengers" must be "many of the passengers".

◦ Corrected sentence: Because of dense fog, the flights were delayed and many of the passengers were stranded.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Because of dense fog," is a proper introductory phrase, since "because of" is followed by a noun.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the flights were delayed and" is a proper passive clause with a plural verb.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "much of the passengers" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• much of the time / money / work but many of the people / students / passengers; most of the can go with both types.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence.

 

This is by far a most useful book on grammar that I have read.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. by far the most useful.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The intensifier "by far" is used with a superlative, and a superlative takes the article "the". "A most useful" is not a proper superlative here, so the correct phrase is "by far the most useful".

◦ Corrected sentence: This is by far the most useful book on grammar that I have read.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "at far the most useful" — the idiom is "by far", not "at far".

 

• Option 3: "by far a much useful" — "much" cannot stand before a positive adjective, and "a" does not form a superlative.

 

• Option 4: No improvement required — incorrect, because "a most useful" does not give the superlative sense that "by far" needs.

 

NOTE

 

• by far the best, by far the largest, far better, much better. "By far" and "far" strengthen a comparative or a superlative, but not a positive adjective.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The police chased (a)/ the fastly moving car (b)/ for many kilometres (c)/ along the highway. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Fastly" is not a word in English. "Fast" is both an adjective and an adverb and never takes "-ly". As a compound adjective before "car", the correct form is "fast-moving".

◦ Corrected sentence: The police chased the fast-moving car for many kilometres along the highway.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The police chased" is proper, since "police" takes a plural verb and the past tense suits the sentence.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "for many kilometres" is a proper prepositional phrase, and "many" goes with the plural "kilometres".

 

• Part (d) is correct — "along the highway" is a proper prepositional phrase of place.

 

NOTE

 

• Adjectives with the same adverb form: fast, hard, late, early, high, near, straight, long, deep — a fast car / runs fast. Adding "-ly" changes the meaning: hardly (barely), lately (recently), highly (very), nearly (almost).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Handloom fabrics are popular (a)/ among tourists because (b)/ their quality is (c)/ far superior than mill-made cloth. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Superior, inferior, senior, junior, prior, preferable are Latin comparatives. They are followed by "to" and never by "than". So "superior than" must be "superior to".

◦ Corrected sentence: Handloom fabrics are popular among tourists because their quality is far superior to mill-made cloth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Handloom fabrics are popular" is a proper plural subject with the correct plural verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "among tourists because" is a proper phrase leading into the clause of reason.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "their quality is" is proper, since the singular verb "is" agrees with "quality".

 

NOTE

 

• superior to, inferior to, senior to, junior to, prior to, preferable to; also prefer A to B — never prefer A than B.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The rescue team (a)/ searched the ruins (b)/ and found an alive kitten (c)/ after two days. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Alive" (like asleep, awake, afraid, alone, ashamed) is a predicative adjective: it is used after a verb, not before a noun. Before a noun, the adjective "living" (or "live") is used. So "an alive kitten" must be "a living kitten", or the sentence can say "a kitten alive".

◦ Corrected sentence: The rescue team searched the ruins and found a living kitten after two days.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The rescue team" is a proper singular collective subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "searched the ruins" is a proper past verb phrase with a correct object.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "after two days." is a proper prepositional phrase of time.

 

NOTE

 

• asleep → a sleeping child; afraid → a frightened child; alone → a lone traveller; alive → a living creature. The predicative forms are used like this: The child is asleep, The kitten was found alive.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Respectable silence (a)/ prevailed in the hall (b)/ as the chief guest (c)/ began his address. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Respectful" means showing respect, while "respectable" means "of good reputation" or "socially acceptable". Silence that shows honour to a speaker is "respectful silence".

◦ Corrected sentence: Respectful silence prevailed in the hall as the chief guest began his address.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "prevailed in the hall" is a proper verb phrase, and the singular verb agrees with the singular subject "silence".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "as the chief guest" is a proper conjunction and subject of the time clause.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "began his address." is a proper past verb phrase with a correct object.

 

NOTE

 

• respectful (showing respect) — a respectful audience, respectful behaviour; respectable (decent, of good standing) — a respectable family, a respectable job; respective (belonging to each) — They went to their respective homes.

question:
Select the correct degree of comparison for the given sentence.

 

This route is (short) than the one we took yesterday.
option_1: This route is short than the one we took yesterday.
option_2: This route is shorter than the one we took yesterday.
option_3: This route is shortest than the one we took yesterday.
option_4: This route is more short than the one we took yesterday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. This route is shorter than the one we took yesterday.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The word "than" shows a comparison between two routes, so the comparative degree is required. "Short" is a one-syllable adjective, so its comparative is formed with "-er": "shorter".

◦ Correct sentence: This route is shorter than the one we took yesterday.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "short than" — the positive degree cannot be followed by "than".

 

• Option 3: "shortest than" — the superlative cannot be followed by "than"; it needs "the" and a group.

 

• Option 4: "more short than" — one-syllable adjectives form the comparative with "-er", and not with "more".

 

NOTE

 

• One syllable: short – shorter – shortest. Long adjectives: more useful – most useful. Two-syllable words ending in "-y" change "y" to "i": busy – busier – busiest.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Please taste the tea and (a)/ tell me whether (b)/ it is (c)/ enough hot for you. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Enough" is placed after an adjective or an adverb, and before a noun. So "enough hot" must be "hot enough".

◦ Corrected sentence: Please taste the tea and tell me whether it is hot enough for you.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Please taste the tea and" is a proper imperative clause.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "tell me whether" is proper, since "whether" suits an indirect question.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "it is" is a proper subject and verb.

 

NOTE

 

• hot enough, old enough, fast enough, well enough (after an adjective or adverb) but enough money, enough time (before a noun).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Among all the entries (a)/ in the competition, her design (b)/ was the most unique (c)/ and creative. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Absolute adjectives — unique, perfect, complete, entire, universal, empty, ideal, supreme — describe a quality that is complete in itself and cannot be compared. "Unique" means "one of a kind", so "the most unique" must be "unique".

◦ Corrected sentence: Among all the entries in the competition, her design was unique and creative.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Among all the entries" is a proper introductory phrase, and "among" suits more than two.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "in the competition, her design" is a proper phrase with a singular subject.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "and creative." is a proper coordinate adjective.

 

NOTE

 

• more perfect, most unique, most complete, more circular, most supreme are incorrect. Use modifiers such as almost / nearly / truly: almost perfect, truly unique.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The farmers do not have many water (a)/ for irrigation (b)/ this summer. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Many" is used with countable plural nouns, while "much" is used with uncountable nouns. "Water" is uncountable, so "many water" must be "much water".

◦ Corrected sentence: The farmers do not have much water for irrigation this summer.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "for irrigation" is a proper prepositional phrase of purpose.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "this summer." is a proper adverbial of time.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "many water" in part (a) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• many books, many people but much water, much time, much money. In negative sentences and questions, "much" is common: We do not have much time, How much water is left?.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The young director is known (a)/ for his bold vision, (b)/ sharp editing and (c)/ an imaginary approach to storytelling. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Imaginary" means "existing only in the imagination, not real" (an imaginary friend), while "imaginative" means "creative and full of original ideas". An approach to storytelling that is creative is "imaginative".

◦ Corrected sentence: The young director is known for his bold vision, sharp editing and an imaginative approach to storytelling.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The young director is known" is a proper singular subject with a correct passive verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "for his bold vision," is a proper prepositional phrase, and "for" follows "known".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "sharp editing and" is a proper noun phrase in the list.

 

NOTE

 

• imaginary (unreal) — imaginary creatures, an imaginary line; imaginative (creative) — an imaginative writer, an imaginative idea; imaginable (that can be imagined) — the best imaginable result.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Of all the participants in (a)/ the marathon, Priya was the faster (b)/ and the most (c)/ determined runner. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Faster" is a comparative, used for two persons. Priya is compared with all the participants, so the superlative "the fastest" is required. It also matches the parallel superlative "the most determined".

◦ Corrected sentence: Of all the participants in the marathon, Priya was the fastest and the most determined runner.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Of all the participants in" is a proper phrase that names the whole group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and the most" is a proper superlative marker that matches the previous adjective.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "determined runner." is a proper adjective + noun phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• Of the two, Priya is the faster but Of all the runners, Priya is the fastest. Two → comparative; more than two → superlative.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Rohit and his family (a)/ stayed near the beach (b)/ in a five stars hotel. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When a number + noun is used as an adjective before a noun, the noun stays singular and is joined by a hyphen. So "a five stars hotel" must be "a five-star hotel".

◦ Corrected sentence: Rohit and his family stayed near the beach in a five-star hotel.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Rohit and his family" is a proper plural subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "stayed near the beach" is a proper past verb phrase with a prepositional phrase of place.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "five stars" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• a five-star hotel but a hotel with five stars; a three-day trip, a two-lane road, a ten-page report, a 500-word essay.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The young runner sprinted swift (a)/ towards the finish line (b)/ and won the (c)/ gold medal. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A verb ("sprinted") is described by an adverb, not by an adjective. "Swift" is an adjective, so it must be changed to the adverb "swiftly".

◦ Corrected sentence: The young runner sprinted swiftly towards the finish line and won the gold medal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "towards the finish line" is a proper prepositional phrase of direction.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and won the" is a proper coordinate verb phrase in the simple past.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "gold medal." is a proper noun phrase, and "gold" acts as a noun modifier.

 

NOTE

 

• She walked slowly, He spoke clearly, They worked carefully. Some adverbs have the same form as the adjective and take no "-ly": run fast, work hard, arrive late, aim high.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Kavita is (a)/ the most experienced (b)/ and respected of (c)/ all other players. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• With a superlative, the words "all other" cannot be used, because the person being described belongs to the group and is not "other". The correct phrase is "of all the players".

◦ Corrected sentence: Kavita is the most experienced and respected of all the players.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Kavita is" is a proper singular subject with the correct verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "the most experienced" is a proper superlative, since "experienced" takes "most".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "and respected of" is a proper coordinate adjective linked to the preceding superlative.

 

NOTE

 

• Superlative + of all the: the best of all the students. Comparative + than all other: better than all other students. Never mix them: the best of all other students is wrong.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

The witness's story (a)/ was hardly credulous, (b)/ so the court (c)/ rejected it. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Credible" means "believable", while "credulous" means "too ready to believe things". A story that the court refuses to accept is not "credible", so "credulous" must be "credible".

◦ Corrected sentence: The witness's story was hardly credible, so the court rejected it.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "The witness's story" is a proper singular subject with a correct possessive.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "so the court" is a proper clause of result.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "rejected it." is a proper past verb phrase with a correct object.

 

NOTE

 

• credible (believable) / credulous (gullible) / creditable (praiseworthy); likewise incredible (unbelievable) / incredulous (unwilling to believe).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

Regular exercise (a)/ is linked to (b)/ a healthiest and happy life. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The superlative "healthiest" is used only when comparison with all others is meant, and it needs "the". Here no comparison is made and the article is "a", so the positive degree "healthy" is required: "a healthy and happy life". It also matches the positive adjective "happy".

◦ Corrected sentence: Regular exercise is linked to a healthy and happy life.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Regular exercise" is a proper singular subject.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is linked to" is a proper passive verb phrase with the correct preposition.

 

• Option (d) No error — cannot be selected, because "a healthiest" in part (c) is incorrect.

 

NOTE

 

• A superlative is used only for comparison with all others — the healthiest person in the family. For a general quality, use the positive: a healthy and happy life, a long and prosperous life.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

There is still a few hope (a)/ that the missing trekkers (b)/ will be found alive (c)/ by the rescue team. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. (a).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Hope" is an uncountable noun, and "a few" is used only with countable plural nouns. The correct quantifier is "a little" (= some, though not much).

◦ Corrected sentence: There is still a little hope that the missing trekkers will be found alive by the rescue team.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (b) is correct — "that the missing trekkers" is a proper noun clause that follows "hope".

 

• Part (c) is correct — "will be found alive" is a proper passive verb phrase, and "alive" correctly follows the verb.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "by the rescue team." is a proper agent phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• a little hope, a little time, a little help but a few chances, a few days, a few friends. little hope = almost none; a little hope = some.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Reading widely improves (a)/ our vocabulary, and (b)/ the more we read, (c)/ better we write. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In the structure "the + comparative …, the + comparative …", both clauses must begin with "the". So "better we write" must be "the better we write".

◦ Corrected sentence: Reading widely improves our vocabulary, and the more we read, the better we write.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Reading widely improves" is proper, since the gerund subject takes a singular verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "our vocabulary, and" is a proper noun phrase with a correct connector.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "the more we read," is a proper first clause of the double-comparative pattern.

 

NOTE

 

• The sooner, the better; The more, the merrier; The higher the price, the lower the demand. In this pattern "the" is an adverb meaning "by how much … by that much".

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error. If the sentence is free from error, select 'No error'.

 

The new employee looked nervous (a)/ but answered every question (b)/ confidently. (c)/ No error (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. (d).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The sentence is grammatically correct. "Looked nervous" uses the linking verb "looked" with an adjective, because it describes the employee. "Answered … confidently" uses an adverb, because it describes the action of answering.

◦ Sentence as given: The new employee looked nervous but answered every question confidently.

 

• "Every question" correctly takes a singular noun, and "but" correctly joins two contrasting predicates of the same subject.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "looked nervous" is right, as a linking verb takes an adjective.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "but answered every question" is proper, since "every" is followed by a singular noun.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "confidently." is a proper adverb that modifies the action verb "answered".

 

NOTE

 

• Do not over-correct: looked nervously would mean "looked around in a nervous manner" (an action). She looked happy (state) but She looked at him happily (action).

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Of the four (a)/ finalists, the former (b)/ was declared the (c)/ winner. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "The former" refers to the first of two things mentioned. Four finalists are named, so the correct word is "the first".

◦ Corrected sentence: Of the four finalists, the first was declared the winner.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Of the four" is a proper phrase that names the group.

 

• Part (c) is correct — "was declared the" is a proper passive verb phrase with the correct article.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "winner." properly completes the noun phrase "the winner".

 

NOTE

 

• former / latter — used for two things only; first / last — used for three or more: Of the four finalists, the first… the last.

question:
Find the part of the sentence that contains an error.

 

Engineers say that the new bridge (a)/ is safe and (b)/ stronger enough to bear (c)/ the weight of heavy trucks. (d)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. (c).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• "Enough" is used with the positive degree of an adjective: "strong enough". It is never used with the comparative, so "stronger enough" must be "strong enough".

◦ Corrected sentence: Engineers say that the new bridge is safe and strong enough to bear the weight of heavy trucks.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part (a) is correct — "Engineers say that the new bridge" is a proper subject with a correct reporting verb.

 

• Part (b) is correct — "is safe and" is a proper singular verb with a coordinate adjective.

 

• Part (d) is correct — "the weight of heavy trucks." is a proper noun phrase.

 

NOTE

 

• strong enough to bear (positive + enough + to), too strong to break, stronger than the old bridge. Never combine the comparative with "enough".
